clue.text: One interrupts composer to state it's really true

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the middle of the composer's name, interrupting it

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer
the Roman numeral for one is I
CAL is an abbreviation of California, a US state

explanation.surface: A soloist cuts in on a composer to insist that what is said is genuinely so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link word here; the definition is the adjective phrase 'really true'.
explanation.definitionFit: Veridical is a formal word for truthful or corresponding to reality, so it describes something genuinely so.

clue.text: One frequents Alabama, another Tennessee

parts.note: the state names are read as spellings: Alabama is full of one letter, A, and Tennessee is full of another, E, both of the same class of letter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests people visiting US states, but the clue is about letters: A occurs four times in Alabama and E four times in Tennessee.
explanation.definitionFit: A and E are both members of the group of letters A, E, I, O, U, as opposed to consonants.

clue.text: Having faith, somewhat obscurely, in God

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Believing in a deity, though only vaguely and partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Relying on someone means trusting or depending on them, which is having faith in them.

clue.text: Host rises to give a hand to farm girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a host is a great number, a myriad
to give a hand is to help, to aid

explanation.surface: A party host gets up to help a girl working on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a person entertaining guests, but it means a multitude. 'rises' turns MYRIAD into DAIRYM; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid is a young woman who milks cows and makes butter on a farm.

clue.text: General Murphy as sound broadcaster ?

indicators.note: sound says the word is what you hear when the phrase before it is spoken

parts.note: general means common, and a murphy is slang for a potato, a tater

explanation.surface: A military man named Murphy acts as a radio presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General Murphy' looks like an army officer; read it as 'common tater' (an ordinary potato; murphy is old slang for a potato, from the Irish surname), which said quickly gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A commentator describes events such as sports matches live on radio or television.

clue.text: Testing situation completed by 18

parts.note: a short word that, finished off by the answer to 18 down written after it, makes the full word for a place where experiments are done; it is also that place's short name

explanation.walkthrough: 18 down is ORATORY, and LAB + ORATORY spells LABORATORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lab, short for laboratory, is a place where tests and experiments are carried out.

clue.text: Surrounded, as end of cake is by cream

indicators.note: the end letter of cake is set within the word for cream, which closes around it

parts.note: the cream of something is the best of it

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word cake

explanation.surface: A cake topped with cream, its edge enclosed by the filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cream' looks like a dairy topping, but it means the finest, BEST; the E from 'end of cake' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Beset means hemmed in or set upon on all sides, as by enemies or troubles.

clue.text: It's elementary when King's in favour

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Something is simple once the monarch approves of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elementary' suggests 'simple', but here it means 'a chemical element'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boron is a chemical element, number 5 in the periodic table, so it belongs among the elements.

clue.text: Only fair to Include also a certain person

indicators.note: one word takes another inside it, including it

parts.note: so-so means only fair, middling
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: It is merely fair to count in a particular individual as well.
explanation.walkthrough: SO-SO is split around AND.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-so is a stand-in for someone not named, an unspecified individual.

clue.text: Perversely start nine or ten trains passing

indicators.note: perversely means contrarily, so the letters are turned into a wrong order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Railway trains run in an awkward order, nine or ten of them going by.
explanation.walkthrough: A double anagram: START + NINE, or alternatively TEN + TRAINS, both rearranged by 'Perversely' give the answer, so 'or ten trains' offers a second route.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means fleeting, lasting only a short time.

clue.text: Orange one for half a sovereign

definitions.meaning: the Prince of Orange who took the English throne in 1688
he reigned jointly with Mary II, making him one of a pair of monarchs

explanation.walkthrough: 'half a sovereign' looks like an old ten-shilling gold coin, but it means one of two joint monarchs (William and Mary).
explanation.definitionFit: William III, Prince of Orange, ruled England jointly with his wife Mary.

clue.text: Major part for her

parts.note: The title role is a woman's name that follows the word Major

explanation.walkthrough: 'Major part' suggests a large role in general; it is the role that completes the title of Shaw's play 'Major ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara Undershaft is the heroine of Shaw's play Major Barbara.

clue.text: The cloth's not here, so set table without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word sits around the other

parts.note: to lay the table is to set it
taken as written

explanation.surface: No tablecloth available, so lay the table bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is the clergy; ordinary church members are where the clergy is not. 'without' means outside: LAY goes round IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are the non-ordained members of a church, as distinct from the clergy.

clue.text: Bad enemies, 25 unloved and vengeful females

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters are put into a corrupted order
love is zero in tennis scores, the letter O, so unloved means that letter is removed

parts.note: the answer to 25 down, a pair of performers

explanation.surface: Wicked foes, a couple without love, and spiteful women.
explanation.walkthrough: DUO (25 down) loses its O to give DU, which is rearranged with ENEMIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eumenides, or Furies, are the avenging goddesses of Greek myth.

clue.text: Flier taking off

parts.note: taking someone off means imitating or mimicking them
a flier is something that flies, a bird

explanation.surface: A plane leaving the runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' suggests a plane's departure; it means mimicking, which this bird is famed for.
explanation.definitionFit: The mockingbird is an American songbird famous for mimicking other birds' calls.

clue.text: What shadow-boxer is, twice?

parts.note: the word means to shadow or follow, and a boxer is a breed of that animal, so one word covers both halves of shadow-boxer

explanation.walkthrough: A shadow-boxer looks like a boxer sparring alone; split it into 'shadow', meaning to follow, and 'boxer', a breed of canine.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, and a boxer is a breed of hound-like pet.

clue.text: Grebes produce note, basic knowledge to countrymen

parts.note: D is a musical note
the ABC of a subject is its basics
hicks are unsophisticated country people

explanation.surface: Water birds give a musical tone and an elementary lesson to rural folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' and 'to' are links. 'countrymen' suggests compatriots, but means rural people.
explanation.definitionFit: Dabchicks are little grebes, small diving water birds.

clue.text: Conceal tiny error occurring in forecast

indicators.note: an error puts the letters of the two preceding words into a mistaken order

explanation.surface: Someone hides a small mistake that crept into the weather report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' looks like a noun in the story but signals the anagram of CONCEAL and TINY.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticyclone is a high-pressure weather system, a feature mentioned in weather forecasts.

clue.text: Scans radar endlessly-could be indicator of trouble ahead

indicators.note: could be says the letters might form something else, rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of radar is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone keeps watching a radar screen for signs of danger approaching.
explanation.walkthrough: RADAR without its end gives RADA, rearranged with SCANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra, the Trojan prophetess never believed, is the name for anyone who foretells disaster.

clue.text: Wide flight-path along Kent coast

parts.note: broad means wide
a flight is a set of stairs

explanation.surface: A broad aircraft route runs down the shoreline of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight-path' reads as an aircraft's route; split it into 'flight', the stairs, and 'path'. Broadstairs is a seaside resort on the Kent coast in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadstairs is a seaside town on the Isle of Thanet in Kent.

clue.text: Chapel sermon, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a small place of private worship
a sermon is an example of formal public speaking, the art of eloquent speech

explanation.definitionFit: An oratory is a small chapel, and oratory is the art of public speaking, which a sermon displays.

clue.text: Anglers' sort of square or circle?

definitions.meaning: a drawing triangle used by those who draw angles
a circle of people is a social group

explanation.walkthrough: 'Anglers' suggests people fishing; it means people drawing angles, who use a set square.
explanation.definitionFit: A set square is a triangular drawing instrument, and a set is a group of people, like a social circle.

clue.text: A cabbage for the walrus, perhaps, but no king

definitions.text: A cabbage for the walrus, perhaps, but no king

parts.words: A cabbage for the walrus, perhaps, but no king
parts.note: Carroll's Walrus wanted to talk of many things, of cabbages and kings; a cabbage is a topic of talk, and a person who is not a king is ruled by one

explanation.walkthrough: From Lewis Carroll's 'The Walrus and the Carpenter': 'The time has come, the Walrus said, to talk of many things... of cabbages and kings.'
explanation.definitionFit: A subject is both a topic of conversation and a person under a monarch's rule.

clue.text: Floor-covering rather unusual in stronghold?

indicators.note: in places the rearranged word inside the other

parts.note: a hug is a strong hold, a tight embrace

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of rather come in an odd order

explanation.surface: A rug that would be out of place in a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stronghold' looks like a fortress; it is a strong hold, an embrace. 'unusual' turns RATHER into EARTHR, which goes inside HUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearthrug is a small mat laid in front of a fireplace.

clue.text: A capital change from Kyoto

indicators.note: a change of letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Japan moved its seat of government from one city to another.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Japan's capital did move from Kyoto to Tokyo in 1868.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan.

clue.text: Extent of first part of day

indicators.note: first says the word for day's opening hours comes at the front

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is the morning portion of the day
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: How much of the morning counts as the start of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: AM stands for the morning hours, before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit means scope or range, the bounds within which something extends.

clue.text: Revolting peasant-or doorman, you say?

definitions.meaning: Wat ... led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381
the doorkeeper of a Masonic lodge, a word spelt like the roofer who lays tiles

explanation.walkthrough: 'you say' points out the doorman's title sounds like a roof-tiler. 'Revolting' means rebelling, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Wat Tyler led the English rebellion of 1381, and a tyler guards the door of a Freemasons' lodge.

clue.text: Many swindled by such a character

definitions.text: Many swindled by such a character

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
rooked means cheated or swindled

explanation.surface: Lots of people have been conned by a dishonest type.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a dishonest character swindles many.
explanation.definitionFit: A crooked character is dishonest, the sort who cheats people out of money.

clue.text: Company of performers?

parts.note: company in the sense of keeping someone company: two performers together form the smallest possible troupe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' suggests a theatre troupe; the old saying 'two's company' makes it a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair of musicians or entertainers performing together.

clue.text: Live in land of poesy, with water supply

parts.note: Ind is a poetic name for India
a well supplies water

explanation.surface: Dwell in the realm of poetry, with a spring for water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. Ind is an archaic, literary name for India.
explanation.definitionFit: To indwell is to dwell within or inhabit, as a spirit does a body.

clue.text: Sort of pen, look

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Pointing out a kind of writing instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' suggests a writing tool, then turns out to be a pigpen too: the whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylo, short for stylograph, is a fountain pen with a fine tubular point.

clue.text: Painter seldom associated with art collection?

indicators.note: a collection gathers the letters together and rearranges them

explanation.surface: An artist rarely linked to a gallery's holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection' looks like an art collection but signals the anagram of SELDOM and ART; 'associated with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a great European painter from before about 1800, or a work by one.
